tb-402-3.question:
A p.d. is applied to a copper wire. Which of the following changes can increase the amount of charge passing through the wire every second?

(1) Increase the applied p.d.

(2) Increase the length of the wire.

(3) Reduce the diameter of the wire.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-402-3.reasoning:
By I =VR, the current through the wire, i.e. the amount of charge passing through each second, increases as the p.d. across the wire increases.

∴ (1) is correct.

By R =ρlA, the resistance of the wire increases as the length of the wire increases.

By I =VR, the current through the wire decreases.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

The cross-sectional area of the wire decreases as the diameter of the wire decreases.

By R =ρlA, the resistance of the wire increases.

By I =VR, the current through the wire decreases.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

Figure g shows the V–I graphs of two resistors X and Y.

The two resistors are then connected together to form a resistor Z. In which region will the V–I graph of Z be if the two resistors are connected in series and in parallel respectively to form Z?

In series

In parallel

M

tb-402-10.reasoning:
The equivalent resistance of resistors connected in series is always higher than the resistance of any single resistor in the series combination. So, by V = IR, its V is higher for the same I. This means its V–I graph is in region K.

The equivalent resistance of resistors connected in parallel is always lower than the resistance of any single resistor in the parallel combination. So, by V = IR, its V is lower for the same I. This means its V–I graph is in region M.

James is given a certain number of identical bulbs and a 6-V battery. When he connects all the bulbs in series to the battery, the current drawn from the battery is 0.15 A. When he connects all the bulbs in parallel, the current drawn from the battery is 2.4 A. Find the number of bulbs.

equivalent resistance = nR

6 = 0.15 × nR (1)

By V = IR,

(1) ÷ (2),
